key_insight: Multimodal LLMs struggle with hospital spatial reasoning, while targeted fine-tuning and GeoJeV’s explicit 3D computation improve benchmark performance.
clinical_relevance: The benchmark tests abilities relevant to navigating hospital spaces and locating equipment, but does not establish safety or effectiveness in clinical use.
method: Created 3,368 questions across eight spatial task types using simulated walkthroughs of 373 hospital-room layouts.
Evaluated 35 multimodal LLMs and fine-tuned two models on 44,750 training questions.
Developed GeoJeV to reconstruct 3D scene memory and incorporate evidence from question-selected spatial operations.
evidence_signal: Best open and proprietary models achieved 45.7% and 53.6% macro accuracy; physicians scored 79.0% on a subset, and GeoJeV ranked highest among evaluated models.
watch_item: Results come from simulated environments; robustness in real hospitals remains unproven, and supplying 3D maps alone did not ensure models used them.
paper_title: Clinical3D-Bench: Evaluating and Improving Spatial Intelligence of Multimodal LLMs in Hospital Environments
